text:
Clayton Keller's season reads like a passer's diary. The Mammoth captain has 29 points in 23 games, and 24 of them are assists. Nineteen came on the power play, which is where Utah runs through him. In his last ten games he has 13 assists and one goal.

The goal total is the strange part. He has 5 goals on 7.7 expected, shooting 8.5% against a typical range near 12%. Goals tend to follow chances, and he still gets them. The other worry is five on five: Utah's shot share is fine with him on, but its expected goals share is 8.6 points worse than when he sits. That is a big swing for a player Evolving-Hockey rated sixth among all forwards last season, though they also noted his results ran ahead of his chances then.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile for setting up shots last season, and that part has not changed. We project him for about 97 points, most of them helpers.
headline: Keller is setting up everybody but himself
